reference_sql:
WITH promo_products AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT product_id
  FROM promotion_products
)
SELECT s.parent_category, SUM(s.net_revenue_eur) AS revenue_eur
FROM sales s
JOIN promo_products pp ON pp.product_id = s.product_id
GROUP BY s.parent_category
alternatives: WITH promo_products AS (SELECT product_id FROM promotion_products GROUP BY product_id) SELECT s.parent_category, SUM(s.net_revenue_eur) AS revenue_eur FROM sales s JOIN promo_products pp ON pp.product_id = s.product_id GROUP BY 1

WITH product_revenue AS (SELECT product_id, parent_category, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS revenue_eur FROM sales GROUP BY product_id, parent_category), promo_products AS (SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM promotion_products) SELECT r.parent_category, SUM(r.revenue_eur) AS revenue_eur FROM product_revenue r JOIN promo_products pp ON pp.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY r.parent_category

other_way.sql: WITH product_revenue AS (SELECT product_id, parent_category, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS revenue_eur FROM sales GROUP BY product_id, parent_category), promo_products AS (SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM promotion_products) SELECT r.parent_category, SUM(r.revenue_eur) AS revenue_eur FROM product_revenue r JOIN promo_products pp ON pp.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY r.parent_category
other_way.tradeoff: Adding up revenue per product before the join also stops the repeats, but the DISTINCT list of products is the smaller fix.
